Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH"
Document applicant: "LEICH und MEHL GmbH"

The difference: "Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH" vs "LEICH und MEHL GmbH". The document omits "und Co." — is that legal-suffix drift or spelling drift? "Co." is part of the company name (like "Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH" vs "Leich und Mehl GmbH"). Hmm.

The rules say: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Genuinely different company names = different-entity.

"Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH" vs "LEICH und MEHL GmbH" — case differences are trivially drift. The omission of "und Co." — is that a genuinely different company or drift? Companies often abbreviate their names on documents. The core company identity "Leich und Mehl" is preserved. This looks like an abbreviation/truncation rather than a different company. In certificate databases, the register often holds the fuller legal name from the OIML-CS database, while the document may abbreviate.

I'd say same-entity, with best_value from register ("Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH") since the register holds the canonical fuller legal name. The rule for same-entity says "best_value" — for number/year it says register's canonical form; for spelling drift presumably the register's form is canonical too. Yes, best_value = register value.

Also note document noise: the document text also contains "Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH" in the embedded HTML comment matching the register exactly, while the human-readable text says "LEICH und MEHL GmbH". That supports same-entity — the metadata agrees with register. The visible body just abbreviates. So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's "Leich und Mehl und Co. GmbH".

One sentence why: The document name is the same firm with case variation and a dropped "und Co." abbreviation; the embedded cert_id metadata confirms the register's fuller name, so it's the same entity.

Output single JSON object.
